arithmetic: The filing prints no explicit gross prior-year movement, so the filing's figure is the p65 gross triangle recomputation over underwriting years 2016-2022 (report year 2024 minus 2): end-2024 minus end-2023 cumulative gross estimate, $000. 2016: 71,439-72,131 = -692; 2017: 110,139-110,913 = -774; 2018: 113,460-113,143 = +317; 2019: 135,488-138,647 = -3,159; 2020: 317,073-324,332 = -7,259; 2021: 523,702-373,107 = +150,595; 2022: 404,010-402,150 = +1,860. Sum +140,888 thousand = +140.888m (deterioration). Adopted +140.888m. Difference 0.000m; tolerance max(0.5, 0.05 x 140.888) = 7.044m; same sign; within tolerance. Check that the 2024 diagonal does not carry the Syndicate 3268 take-on: the whole-diagonal change is 2,287,738 - 1,703,243 (72,131+110,913+113,143+138,647+324,332+373,107+402,150+168,820) = 584,495. Gross claims incurred in 2024 are 284,299 paid + 323,448 change in provision = 607,747 (p27; p101 'Claims incurred in the year 607,747'). If the end-2023 diagonal excluded 3268, the change would be at least 284,299 + (1,009,594 - 600,368) = 693,525. If 3268 is included in both diagonals (restated), it is about 284,299 + (1,009,594 - 696,978) = 596,915. The observed 584,495 fits the restated basis. The net table (p67) agrees: its diagonal change is 1,563,703 - 1,204,086 = 359,617, against net incurred of 377,448 (p101).
basis_check: p65 is headed 'Analysis of claims development - gross of reinsurance'. The companion p67 'net of reinsurance' table recomputes for the same years to -1,326 -7,389 +7,875 -1,472 -5,115 +33,656 -16,316 = +9,913 thousand (+9.913m), so the adopted 140.888m is the gross figure, not net. Consistent with the loader's gross basis.
page_binding_check: Yes. This is a single-syndicate report: p9 names IQUW Syndicate Management Limited as managing agent of Syndicate 1856, and every text page is footed 'Reports & Accounts Syndicate 1856' (p65 is printed page 32). Syndicate 218 appears only in a director's title (p15). The p63 note says the pre-2022 development data include Syndicate 3268, which was reinsured into 1856 with effect from 1 January 2024. Those liabilities were 1856's own during 2024; this is not a companion syndicate's figure. The even pages of the converted PDF carry no text.
triangle_arithmetic: Printed gross triangle p65, $000, underwriting years 2016-2024 as columns. Every cell equals the pack's stored grid. The row totals (e.g. Two years later 1,935,103; Three years later 1,319,546; Four years later 781,065) and the 'Current estimate of cumulative claims' row confirm the column alignment. Last diagonal (end 2024) minus previous diagonal (end 2023): 2016 (8 vs 7 years later) 71,439-72,131 = -692; 2017 (7 vs 6) 110,139-110,913 = -774; 2018 (6 vs 5) 113,460-113,143 = +317; 2019 (5 vs 4) 135,488-138,647 = -3,159; 2020 (4 vs 3) 317,073-324,332 = -7,259; 2021 (3 vs 2) 523,702-373,107 = +150,595; 2022 (2 vs 1) 404,010-402,150 = +1,860. Sum +140,888 thousand = +140.888m. The two most recent underwriting years are excluded: 2023 (293,479-168,820 = +124,659) and 2024 (318,948).
reasoning: No gross prior-year movement is printed anywhere. The managing agent's report (p9) mentions strengthening of Russia-Ukraine reserves but gives no figure. p13's Russia-Ukraine gross booked ultimates ($230.6m, 2023: $64.9m, inclusive of reinstatement premiums) cover one event, not all prior years. So under the protocol the filing's figure is the recomputation from the printed gross triangle: +140.888m, identical to the adopted value. It excludes the two most recent underwriting years and is gross (the net recomputation is +9.913m). One possible conflict was checked: the +150,595 jump in the 2021 column in the year Syndicate 3268 was reinsured in. p63 says the development data include 3268's data. Both the gross and net diagonal changes reconcile to 2024 claims incurred only if 3268 is in both diagonals. So the figure does not carry the 96,610 take-on. The jump sits in 2021, one of the years p13 says are exposed to Russia-Ukraine, and the net 2021 change is only +33,656. Verdict: correct. The model's own reading (131.906m) was overridden by the triangle route and is not the adopted figure. Opening reserves: the filing prints gross 'At 1 January 2024 600,368' (p101), equal to the 31 December 2023 claims outstanding of 600,368 on p33. The adopted 696.978m is 600,368 plus the p101 row 'RITC from Syndicate 3268 96,610', the register's take-on adjustment. It is therefore 16.1% above the printed opening (outside 2%), but agrees exactly with opening plus take-on. A p101 footnote says the 1 January 2024 balance includes the 3268 RITC; that contradicts the table's own rows, where the RITC is a separate in-year line.
